lead: Someone has stolen the mayor's car.
explanation: Active present perfect (has stolen) becomes passive: has been stolen.

lead: 'I broke the window,' said the boy.
explanation: admit + -ing (optionally 'to'): admitted breaking / admitted to breaking.

lead: It isn't necessary for you to bring any food.
explanation: needn't (need not) = it isn't necessary. Do not confuse with mustn't (prohibition).

lead: She started working here five years ago.
explanation: Action starting in the past and continuing: has been working (present perfect continuous).

lead: I haven't seen such a good film for ages.
sentence: It was ___ I had seen for ages.
explanation: Not…such a good film for ages = the best film (I had seen) for ages.

lead: 'Don't touch the paintings,' the guard warned us.
explanation: Negative commands are reported with not + to-infinitive: warned us not to touch.

lead: He couldn't swim until he was twenty.
sentence: He ___ swim until he was twenty.
explanation: was unable to = couldn't (general ability in the past).

lead: The suitcase was so heavy that I couldn't lift it.
sentence: It was ___ suitcase that I couldn't lift it.
explanation: so + adjective becomes such (+a) + adjective + noun: such a heavy suitcase.

lead: I'd love to be on a beach now.
explanation: wish + past (subjunctive were): I wish I were. 'was' is informal — only 'were' fits the keyword.

lead: People say the castle is haunted.
explanation: People say → It is said… / The castle is said to be…

lead: Although he is rich, he lives very simply.
explanation: Although he may be rich → Rich as (he) may be — the inverted concession pattern.

lead: She prefers reading to watching television.
explanation: prefer X to Y = would rather do X than do Y.

lead: It was a mistake to sell the boat.
explanation: should/shouldn't have + past participle criticises a past action.

lead: They won't allow you to enter without a ticket.
explanation: allow somebody to do → be allowed to do: won't be allowed to enter.

lead: He didn't pass the exam because he hadn't studied.
sentence: If he ___ , he would have passed the exam.
explanation: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + participle.

lead: 'I'll call you as soon as I land,' she said.
sentence: She promised ___ as soon as she landed.
explanation: Reported promise: promised to call (me); pronouns shift.

lead: My father repaired the roof himself.
explanation: have something done = arrange for it to be done by someone else: had the roof repaired.

lead: She moved to Paris and now finds the pace normal.
sentence: She ___ the pace of life in Paris.
explanation: get used to / be used to + -ing or noun: is now used to. 'got used to' also fits if the process is complete.

lead: How much does a yearly membership cost?
sentence: How much ___ pay for a yearly membership?
explanation: have to for external obligation: How much do you have to pay?

lead: They left the party early because it was boring.
sentence: The party was ___ that they left early.
explanation: so + adjective + that-clause: so boring that they left.

lead: I last saw him in March.
explanation: Present perfect with since + point in time: haven't seen him since (March).

lead: Nobody in the class is as tall as Petra.
explanation: X is taller than everyone = X is the tallest (person).

lead: 'Have you finished the report?' the manager asked her.
explanation: Yes/no questions are reported with if/whether + statement word order.

lead: You can borrow the car as long as you drive carefully.
sentence: You can borrow the car ___ carefully.
explanation: provided (that) introduces the condition: provided you drive carefully.

lead: The film was so long that we missed the last bus.
sentence: It was ___ that we missed the last bus.
explanation: so long (a film) → such a long film.

lead: I don't usually drink coffee at night.
explanation: be (not) used to = (not) accustomed to: I'm not used to coffee at night.

lead: The mechanic is servicing my car tomorrow.
explanation: Arranged service: have/get something done — having my car serviced.

lead: He spoke so quickly that nobody understood him.
sentence: He spoke ___ for anybody to understand him.
explanation: so quickly that nobody understood = too quickly (for anybody) to understand.

lead: It's a pity I didn't bring an umbrella.
explanation: Regret about the past: wish + past perfect — I wish I had brought.

lead: 'We're selling the house,' they announced.
sentence: They announced that ___ selling the house.
explanation: we → they; present continuous → past continuous: they were selling.

lead: I'm sure he isn't in Spain — he was here this morning.
sentence: He ___ in Spain — he was here this morning.
explanation: can't be = certainty that something is impossible (present).

lead: They say this forest is three hundred years old.
sentence: This forest ___ three hundred years old.
explanation: They say → is said to be / is thought to be; with keyword THOUGHT: is thought to be.

lead: I only understood the joke much later.
explanation: After 'only + time phrase' at the front, invert: Only much later did I understand.

lead: Someone should test this water regularly.
explanation: should test → should be tested (modal + be + participle).

lead: 'I'm sorry I shouted at you,' he said.
explanation: apologise for doing something: apologised for shouting.

lead: There were fewer people at the concert than expected.
sentence: There weren't ___ at the concert as expected.
explanation: fewer than expected = not as many (people) as expected.

lead: We couldn't find the museum anywhere.
explanation: Nowhere + auxiliary + subject: Nowhere could we find the museum.

lead: She'll be at work, so she won't answer the door.
sentence: She'll be at work, so ___ answer the door.
explanation: won't be able to = future inability.

lead: 'You've stolen my idea!' he said to her.
explanation: accuse somebody OF doing something.

lead: I'm afraid this is the last tin of paint we have.
hint: run out of = have none left
explanation: run out of = have no more of something left.

lead: It's a pity you didn't tell me earlier.
explanation: should/ought to have + participle expresses past regret/advice.

lead: The train takes two hours to get there; the plane takes thirty minutes.
explanation: twice as fast as = half the time of.

lead: He'd rather not discuss the matter.
explanation: would prefer + not + to-infinitive: prefer not to discuss.

lead: The company denied that it had polluted the river.
explanation: deny + -ing (or having + past participle): denied polluting.

lead: 'I'll finish the essay by Friday,' I said.
explanation: commit oneself TO + -ing: committed myself to finishing.

lead: People think she was the best singer of her generation.
sentence: She ___ the best singer of her generation.
explanation: A present belief about a past event uses is thought to have + participle.

lead: It's possible that she forgot about the meeting.
explanation: may/might have + participle = possibility in the past.

lead: As soon as he sat down, the phone rang.
explanation: No sooner + had + subject + participle … than…: No sooner had he sat down (than the phone rang).

lead: I want to go somewhere where nobody knows me.
sentence: I want to go ___ nobody knows me.
explanation: 'somewhere where' = a place in which.

lead: We couldn't go out because of the heavy rain.
explanation: prevent somebody FROM doing something.

lead: 'Let's have a barbecue,' said Dan.
explanation: suggest + -ing (or suggest that + clause): suggested having.

lead: People believe the two paintings are forgeries.
explanation: X is/are believed to be…

lead: This is the worst traffic I've ever experienced.
explanation: Never before + have + subject + participle: Never have I experienced.

lead: The doctor said that he should take a complete rest.
sentence: The doctor advised ___ a complete rest.
explanation: say + should → advise + object + to-infinitive: advised him to take.

lead: Their wedding will take place in June.
explanation: Weddings/concerts are held: will be held (in June).

lead: He was in the habit of jogging every morning.
explanation: be used to + -ing = be in the habit of: was used to jogging.

lead: The flat was too small for their growing family.
sentence: The flat wasn't ___ for their growing family.
explanation: too small = not big enough.

lead: 'You mustn't run near the pool,' the lifeguard told the children.
sentence: The lifeguard told the children ___ near the pool.
explanation: told + object + not to + infinitive.

lead: Only after reading the letter twice did it make sense.
sentence: The letter ___ sense until it had been read twice.
explanation: It made sense only after two readings = it didn't make sense until it had been read twice.

lead: Both sisters play the violin beautifully.
sentence: The sisters ___ play the violin beautifully.
explanation: Both (the) sisters… / The sisters both… — with the given frame, 'both' precedes the verb.

lead: It was unfair of the referee to send him off.
explanation: shouldn't have + participle criticises a past action.

lead: I would love to afford a bigger flat.
explanation: wish + subject + could = regret about ability/possibility.

lead: They chose her for the lead role because of her voice.
sentence: Her voice was ___ for the lead role.
explanation: the reason (why/that) + clause: the reason (why) she was chosen.
accept: the reason why she was chosen

lead: We got to the airport late and missed the flight.
sentence: If we had got to the airport earlier, we ___ the flight.
explanation: If + past perfect, would(n't) have + participle.

lead: My advice is to check the contract carefully.
explanation: had better + infinitive (without to): had better check.

lead: 'Can you open the door for me?' she asked me.
sentence: She asked ___ the door for her.
explanation: ask somebody TO do something: asked me to open.

lead: Everybody says he is the best dentist in town.
sentence: He ___ the best dentist in town.
explanation: be supposed to be = generally believed to be.

lead: The lecture was cancelled because nobody came.
explanation: because so few people came = because hardly anybody came.

lead: He finally managed to solve the puzzle.
explanation: manage to do = be able to do.

lead: The soup needed a bit of salt.
explanation: needed a bit of salt = didn't have enough (salt).

lead: 'I didn't write the graffiti,' the teenager said.
explanation: deny + -ing (or having + participle).

lead: We took a spare tyre in case the journey went wrong.
sentence: We took a spare tyre ___ went wrong.
explanation: in case + clause = as a precaution because something might happen.

lead: It's cheaper to travel off-peak.
sentence: Travel is ___ if you go off-peak.
explanation: cheaper = less expensive.

lead: He started playing golf at the age of six.
sentence: He ___ golf at the age of six.
explanation: take up = start (a hobby/sport): took up golf.

lead: I regret telling her the secret.
explanation: I regret -ing = I shouldn't have + participle.

lead: 'Would you like me to carry that?' he offered.
explanation: offer to do something: offered to carry.

lead: The plane had just taken off when the warning light appeared.
sentence: The plane had ___ when the warning light appeared.
explanation: had just + participle = a very short time before.

lead: Her French improved because she lived in Lyon.
sentence: Her French improved as ___ in Lyon.
explanation: as a result of + noun/-ing: as a result of living.

lead: You can't park here — it's forbidden.
explanation: mustn't = it is forbidden (not: don't have to).

lead: The painter worked for three weeks on the mural.
explanation: spend + time + -ing: spent over three weeks (working on it).

lead: 'I've never been to Asia,' she told me.
sentence: She told me that ___ to Asia.
explanation: Present perfect shifts to past perfect: she had never been.

lead: His salary is low, but he enjoys his work.
explanation: …though his salary is low — 'though' links the concession.

lead: I can't wait for the holidays to begin.
explanation: look forward TO + -ing/noun: looking forward to the holidays beginning.

lead: Nobody can deny that he works hard.
explanation: deny that + clause, or deny + -ing: deny his working (formal).

lead: I got used to night shifts after a month.
sentence: After a month, I ___ night shifts.
explanation: After a period: be used to (state) or had got used to (achievement).

lead: There's no milk left in the fridge.
explanation: run out of = have none left.

lead: Cars must not exceed 30 km/h in this zone.
explanation: must not (mustn't) + infinitive for prohibition.

lead: We expect to announce the winner tomorrow.
explanation: We expect to announce X → X is expected to be announced.

lead: 'Could you pass the salt?' said my aunt to me.
explanation: Reported request: asked me to pass.

lead: He was driving too fast, so he crashed.
sentence: He wouldn't have crashed if he ___ so fast.
explanation: If + past perfect continuous: hadn't been driving.

lead: You must sign the form in ink.
explanation: sign the form in ink → the form must be signed in ink.

lead: That's the school where my mother teaches.
explanation: the school in which my mother teaches = where my mother teaches.

lead: She got up early so that she wouldn't miss the train.
sentence: She got up early ___ the train.
explanation: so as not to / in order not to + infinitive express negative purpose.

lead: I'm sure the tickets are expensive this year.
explanation: must be = I'm sure it is (deduction).

lead: The famine was caused by a long drought.
explanation: A causes B = A results in B.

lead: 'Would you like to join us for dinner?' they asked him.
answer: invited him to join them for
explanation: invite somebody TO do something: invited him to join them.

lead: I haven't enjoyed myself so much for years.
sentence: It's ___ I've enjoyed myself so much.
explanation: It's years since + past simple = I haven't…for years.

lead: The athlete denied taking performance-enhancing drugs.
explanation: deny + having + past participle (or deny taking).

lead: You need to renew your passport before June.
explanation: need + -ing = need to be + participle: needs renewing.

lead: Despite his injury, he finished the marathon.
explanation: in spite of + noun/-ing: In spite of his injury.

lead: People claim that this juice cures colds.
explanation: X is claimed to + infinitive.

lead: He is so impatient that he never reads instructions.
explanation: so impatient that he never reads = too impatient to read.

lead: They say the new bridge will cut journey times in half.
sentence: Journey times ___ in half by the new bridge.
explanation: X is said to be + participle: journey times are said to be cut.

lead: I'd rather you didn't tell anyone about this.
explanation: keep something to yourself = not tell anyone.

lead: The committee is unlikely to change the rules.
sentence: ___ that the committee will change the rules.
explanation: Impersonal it: It is unlikely that…

lead: 'Have you seen my keys anywhere?' he asked us.
sentence: He asked us ___ seen his keys anywhere.
explanation: if/whether + subject + had + participle: whether we had seen.

lead: They don't let visitors feed the animals.
explanation: let somebody do → be allowed to do: are not allowed to feed.

lead: He lost his job because he kept arriving late.
sentence: If he hadn't kept arriving late, he ___ his job.
explanation: If + past perfect, would(n't) have + participle.

lead: 'I'm sorry I was rude to your sister,' Maria said.
sentence: Maria apologised ___ rude to my sister.
explanation: apologise for + -ing (or having + participle for the earlier action).

lead: You won't get a seat unless you book.
explanation: unless you book = without booking.

lead: She speaks French fluently; she also speaks Russian.
sentence: She speaks French fluently and, ___, Russian.
explanation: in addition adds a parallel fact: and, in addition, Russian.

lead: The hotel was further from the beach than we expected.
answer: as close to the beach as
explanation: further than expected = not as close as expected.

lead: It's forbidden to use mobile phones in the exam.
explanation: mustn't + be + participle: mustn't be used.

lead: My grandfather planted all these apple trees.
sentence: My grandfather is the ___ all these apple trees.
explanation: 'the one who planted' identifies the agent with a relative clause.

lead: As soon as the results were announced, people started celebrating.
sentence: The results had ___ people started celebrating.
explanation: No sooner had the results been announced than… — reordered to fit the frame.

lead: The tickets were so expensive that we didn't buy any.
sentence: They were ___ that we didn't buy any.
explanation: so expensive (tickets) → such expensive tickets (no article with plural).

lead: 'I may be late tonight,' my wife said.
sentence: My wife said ___ late that night.
explanation: may often backshifts to might: she might be late.

lead: The doctor made me promise to do the exercises daily.
answer: got me to promise to do
explanation: get somebody TO do something = make/persuade them: got me to promise.

lead: It wasn't necessary for her to cook — we ate out.
explanation: needn't have + participle = it wasn't necessary, but it happened; 'we ate out' shows the cooking served no purpose.

lead: His trainers were so worn out that they had holes in them.
sentence: His trainers were ___ that they had holes in them.
explanation: so worn out = in such bad condition.

lead: I'd prefer you to arrive before eight.
explanation: would rather + subject + past simple: I'd rather you arrived.

lead: The rescue team managed to reach the village by helicopter.
sentence: The rescue team ___ reaching the village by helicopter.
explanation: manage to do = succeed IN doing.

lead: It took me two hours to assemble the wardrobe.
sentence: I ___ two hours assembling the wardrobe.
explanation: it took + time + to do = subject + spent + time + -ing.
